doc: FBL 0.9's grammar family (section 4.9) on Turtle with LF endings: two prefix directives, a resource over three lines with a comment above it, a resource with a trailing comment, and a statement with a blank-node subject that no rule reads. A set, a refused set, an add and a removal, each followed by its undo, so every step starts from the input. The partial reading of a body that does not parse is in w3c-turtle-grammar-partial/.

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read.
A set replaces the label's group `value` inside its quotes, the string token's span narrowed by `match`; the trailing comment on the line is kept (FBL 4.9, 6.3).
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
A value that would not read back as the label is refused: written as it is, the quote inside it would end the string token, so the statement would no longer parse (FBL 4.9). Nothing is written.
steps.refused: The new label would not read back from the Turtle text.

steps.doc: An add after the last resource: on a line of its own after ex:bob's line span, which holds its trailing comment, from the rule's emit with the body's LF. The blank-node statement after it is no resource, so it is not followed (FBL 6.3, grammar).
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
A removal takes the statement's line span: its three lines, the leading comment directly above it and its line ending. The blank line before it stays (FBL 4.1.1, 6.3).
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
